Planning for round 373 is done and the decision is **CONTINUE**. I made no changes under `store/`; it is still clean at `4900b83`.

**Round 372 accepted:** C passed all 10 rows with browser verification and 0 bugs, and gate 372 published `4900b83`, the new baseline. PERF-11c-ii-a is marked done. I archived the old task as `tasks/round-372.md` (identical copy). The round's Low findings are deferred or closed, and the gate's architecture note is recorded as a signal, not a task.

**Round 373 = PERF-11c-ii-b.** The committed status line moves out of the shared workspace context into the existing status store. Today one status message re-renders about 70 components; afterwards it re-renders only the status line. What the user sees and hears does not change. Root has not answered the architecture checkpoint request, so I applied the option the backlog already recorded and ruled the open questions in the task myself.

I built and tested a full sketch of the change, and A applies it as a patch (`b-round-372/sketch.patch.txt`):
- **Tests:** typecheck and Biome are clean, and the full suite passes (252 files, 3,703 tests).
- **First sketch:** it had 6 failures.
  - Five were tests that used a status message to force re-renders, which no longer happens. They now use a different trigger and gained asserts; no assertion was removed.
  - One was a real behaviour change: clicking the ruler while stopped showed the wrong status text. A one-line reorder in `playFrom` fixes it.
- **Perf on a production build:** every assert passes and Play/Stop stay at 11 components. With the round-359 test change that forces status writes during Play, Play now renders 12 components instead of 99. That is the measured win.
- **Mutants:** all six deliberate code breakages turn tests red.
- **tech-lead review:**
  - The one blocking finding was a checksum file I wrote while a test mutation was still applied to my copy. It is regenerated and checked against a fresh apply of the patch.
  - One Medium is ruled an accepted change, because it has no real user path: a status line written in the same update as a gesture refusal is now kept after release. Its two test rows go to the next stage, PERF-11c-iii.

C checks in the browser at both viewports, comparing status texts and screen-reader updates against the baseline. C also re-runs the mutants and perf, and checks the auth guard on anonymous `/studio-lab` and the purchased-track page.

**Problems on my side:** two of my perf runs were invalid because my copy method dropped `public/middle-east.mp3` (tracked in git but matched by `.gitignore`). The task now tells C to copy with `cp -a`. I deleted my 800 MB of scratch copies after saving everything the task cites.

**Order after this round:** REGRESSION first if round 374 is planned on or after 2026-11-08, then PERF-11c-iii, then the rest of the existing queue unchanged.

**Advisor:** available, and used twice. Its first-call advice ruled out dispatching without a sketch. Its second call led to fixing a browser-test row I hadn't checked in the browser, two scripts that pointed at the deleted copies, and missing file-existence checks.

Files are in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `current-task.md`
- `b-round-372.md`
- `b-next.json`
- `backlog.json` (now v338)
- `feature-status.md`
- `b-round-372/` (the sketch, review, claims, mutants and perf logs)
